about_hero_lede: OpenFootball is a project that simulates the real world of football and helps predict results, player transfers and careers.
about_hero_text: Clubs, leagues, players, transfers, finances and reputations all move on their own. You explore the world; the engine plays the football.
about_what_lede: A football world simulator, not another manager game.
about_what_p1: Open Football simulates clubs, leagues, matches, players, transfers, reputations, finances and long-term football dynamics, with no manual match control.
about_what_p2: Everything sits in one connected ecosystem: a transfer changes a career, a career changes a squad, and a squad changes the league table. Matches are resolved by the engine, never by your input.
about_feature_world: Countries, leagues and clubs in one hierarchy
about_feature_match: Match engine with detailed match pages
about_feature_market: Transfers, loans, contracts and club finances
about_feature_ui: Web interface for desktop and mobile
about_feature_cpu: Scales across every CPU core you have
about_how_lede: Run one file, press Process, watch the seasons pass.
about_how_p1: A release is a single self-contained binary: the simulator and the web application in one file. Start it and your browser opens on the world.
about_step_run_note: No install, no runtime to set up, no account.
about_step_load_note: Countries, clubs, squads and players are built in memory at startup.
about_step_move_note: Send anyone to any club at any moment — a transfer or a loan, no negotiation, no fee.
about_step_process_note: Every click moves the calendar on. Or go on holiday and let ten years run in one go.
about_step_close_note: The world ends with the process. Nothing is written to disk.
about_memory_text: There are no save files. The whole football world exists only while the app is running. Close it and the next launch begins a fresh world from the same database.
about_local_title: Run it on your own machine
about_local_text: Download a release, run it, and open the address in your browser. On a remote server, use that server's address with the same port.
about_local_note: Open Football uses every core it can find. It has been tested on machines with 256 CPU cores and still runs comfortably on a laptop.
about_why_lede: I was tired of relearning the same game every year.
about_why_p1: Football Manager changes its interface, its editor workflow and its database format with almost every release, and the work you did last year has to be done again.
about_why_p2: Open Football keeps a stable shape instead. The interface and the data model stay familiar, while the simulation logic, the mechanics and the football intelligence keep improving.
about_why_p3: It is also a laboratory. Move any player to any club, run the simulation, and see what the squad, the tactics, the finances and the match engine make of it: a realistic rebuild, a wonderkid in a stronger league, or Messi at Wolverhampton.
about_question_1: Which club becomes dominant after twenty simulated seasons?
about_question_2: How does a single transfer reshape a career and a club's future?
about_question_3: Can data-driven simulation produce believable tables and results?
about_question_4: What happens when a whole football world keeps running without you?
about_data_text: Club data, player details, league structures and country data live in their own repository, so the football world can improve without touching the simulator. Pull requests are welcome.
about_me_text: I build Open Football on my own, in evenings and at weekends. Found a bug, want a league added, or want to argue about the match engine? Write to me, I read everything.
